title: Experimental Kernel Stability Matrix and Run Manifest
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary
======
This page defines the Experimental Kernel Stability Matrix and an associated run manifest used by the runtime, kernel, profiling, and benchmarking teams to systematically exercise kernel changes across production-like axes (model variants, quantization modes, sequence shapes, batching profiles, and hardware families). The intent is to provide a single-source-of-truth experiment catalog that: 
- Produces repeatable telemetry for stability/latency regressions
- Surfaces cross-layer interactions (KV cache, prefetch, schedule handoffs)
- Ties profiling artifacts to benchmark runs and release notes

Scope and goals
----------------
Scope:
- Controlled experiments for kernel and scheduler changes impacting inference runtime behavior.
- Not intended for full production canaries; those live in the release canary matrix.

Goals:
1) Detect kernel regressions before canary release by exercising representative fidelity points.
2) Produce annotated traces and profiling artifacts that map directly to performance/regression triage playbooks.
3) Provide a prioritized run-order and clear pass/fail criteria that teams can apply in CI and in lab runs.

Matrix concept and axes
-----------------------
We represent experiments as rows in the stability matrix. Each row is a single run configuration (manifest) and includes the following canonical axes:
- kernel_build: short tag for the compiled kernel set under test (e.g. k1.2026-02-05-rc3)
- model_variant: model name + size + tokenizer (e.g. openlm-mini-1B-v2, or redwood-1.3B-finetune)
- quant_mode: fp16 | int8 | q4_0 | q4_1 | q5_0
- hw_target: A100-80GB, H100-80GB, GPUTronX-64GB
- sequence_profile: short | median | long (see "Sequence blocks" table)
- batch_shape: continuous | bursty | single-token-heavy
- admission_profile: normal | preemptive | low_priority
- fidelity_flags: runtime flags that change fallback/kv behavior (e.g. async_prefetch=on, kv_persistence=sticky)
- pass_criteria: numeric SLOs and signal thresholds for this experiment

Example experiment row (table-friendly text)
------------------------------------------------
| row_id | kernel_build | model_variant | quant_mode | hw_target   | seq_profile | batch_shape | admission | fidelity_flags | pass_criteria |
| ESM-101 | k1.2026-02-05-rc3 | redwood-1.3B-finetune | fp16 | A100-80GB | median | continuous | normal | async_prefetch=on;kv_persistence=sticky | p50 < 28ms; p95 < 120ms; error_rate < 0.3% |

Sequence blocks (concrete shapes)
----------------------------------
- short: 8–32 tokens, typical chat assistant system+turns.
- median: 64–256 tokens, mid-length completion workload.
- long: 512–2048 tokens, long-form generation stress.

Run manifest schema (human-readable)
------------------------------------
Each JSON/YAML manifest used by the CI runner must include the following top-level fields (example below):

Example manifest (YAML snippet)
------------------------------
```yaml
id: ESM-101
kernel_build: k1.2026-02-05-rc3
model_variant: redwood-1.3B-finetune
quant_mode: fp16
hw_target: A100-80GB
sequence_profile: median
batch_shape: continuous
admission_profile: normal
fidelity_flags:
  - async_prefetch: true
  - kv_persistence: sticky
request_mix: |
  - 70% text-generation (n=1)
  - 20% chat (n=2 turns)
  - 10% embeddings (small)
metrics_export: prometheus,tracejson
artifacts:
  - perf-profile: /artifacts/esm-101/perf.pb.gz
  - trace: /artifacts/esm-101/trace.jsonl
pass_criteria:
  p50_latency_ms: 28
  p95_latency_ms: 120
  error_rate_pct: 0.3
```

Execution and instrumentation guidelines
----------------------------------------
1) Environment isolation: use dedicated test pool or namespace to avoid noisy neighbors. Document the pool id in the manifest.
2) Warmup: run a 10-minute warmup per row to stabilize kernels and KV caches. Capture pre- and post-warmup traces.
3) Telemetry levels: always enable kernel-level telemetry, request-level tracing, and GC/memory summaries. Use the profiling tag: "esm:row-id" for all exported signals.
4) Artifact naming: follow the artifact prefix convention: <row_id>/<kernel_build>/<hw_target>/
5) Repeats: run each row at least 3 independent times; compute median of medians for stable metrics.

Pass / fail and triage flow
----------------------------
- Automated pass/fail: CI runner evaluates pass_criteria after the median of runs. If any criterion fails, the entire row is marked failed and artifacts are uploaded to the experiment bucket.
- Triage steps on failure:
  1. Confirm environment (pool id, driver/kernel versions) against the manifest.
  2. Load last-good baseline artifact (baseline row id noted in matrix) and replay with the same trace.
  3. Run the profiler diff (script: tooling/esm/profiler-diff.sh) to generate a delta report.
  4. If regression maps to kernel latency (vs. scheduling), open a Kernel Regression Triage ticket and run the controlled-perturbation playbook (link in related_pages).

Integrations with other artifacts
--------------------------------
- Benchmarking suite: each row references a canonical bench workload id (bench-id) used by our throughput and cost simulations. Add bench-id to manifest when exporting to the benchmark catalog.
- Release notes: adds a short section for any failing rows that were run against release candidates. Use the release_notes tag in the manifest for automated aggregation.
- Profiling playbook: row artifacts feed directly into the profiling playbook’s replay harness. Include the sample-rate and trace-filter used.

Default run prioritization and scheduling rules
------------------------------------------------
We prioritize rows with the highest customer impact first:
1) Model families that are in production for top-20 customers
2) Quantization modes in active use (int8, q4_1)
3) Hardware families with active capacity commitments
4) Any kernel builds that change prefetch/prefetch eviction logic

Guardrails and noise budgeting
-----------------------------
- Define a noise budget per row (default: 5% for p95 latency). If observed within budget across repeats, mark as flaky rather than failed.
- Annotate known-noise sources in the manifest (network jitter, shared-NVLink traffic, scheduled maintenance windows).

Operational runbook excerpts (condensed)
---------------------------------------
1) If a run fails with intermittent GPU watchdog resets:
   a) Verify driver and BIOS match matrix-approved list.
   b) Capture core dump and log a kernel-watchdog incident.
   c) Re-run on isolated node; mark row as blocked until hardware is remediated.
2) If p95 deviates but p50 is stable:
   a) Check batch_shape and admission_profile for bursty spikes.
   b) Run a co-located latency corridor test (tool: tooling/esm/latency-corridor.sh).
   c) If batch-induced, add 'burst-hedge' policy to fidelity_flags and re-run.

Example triage table (quick reference)
-------------------------------------
| symptom | likely layer | first artifact to check | action |
| "p50 up, p95 up" | kernel scheduling or kernel op cost | perf.pb.gz, kernel-op-latency.csv | run profiler-diff, isolate kernel-builds |
| "high error rate (5%)" | model conversion/quant mismatch | model-checksum.txt, trace.jsonl | verify quant metadata, re-quantize model |
| "watchdog reset" | hardware/driver | dmesg, nvml logs | escalate to infra SRE, run hardware repro |

Retention and artifact storage policy
-------------------------------------
- Artifacts for passed rows: keep 30 days.
- Artifacts for failed rows: keep 365 days and pin in the experiment bucket.
- Golden baselines: keep indefinitely, rotate when a new release candidate is promoted and validated.

How this page fits into the org
-------------------------------
Primary owners: Kernel team (owners: @kernel-platform), Runtime performance (owners: @runtime-perf).
Secondary: Profiling team, Benchmarking, Release Engineering.
For urgent regressions, follow the incident path described in /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runbooks/runtime-incident-orchestration-and-capacity-decision-matrix-2026.json

Appendix: Quick commands and helper scripts
------------------------------------------
- Run a single manifest locally (example):
  ./tooling/esm/run_manifest.sh --manifest manifests/esm-101.yaml --pool test-pool-12

- Diff two profiles:
  ./tooling/esm/profiler-diff.sh /artifacts/esm-101/perf.pb.gz /artifacts/baseline-0401/perf.pb.gz --output /tmp/diff.html

- Generate manifest from bench-id:
  python tooling/esm/generate_manifest.py --bench-id bench-7 --kernel k1.latest --out manifests/auto-esm-###.yaml
